Table of polygon predictions

Source: R/prediction_table.R
to_table.RiskMap_prediction.Rd

Formats the polygon summaries returned by predict.RiskMap() as a presentation-ready table, with one row per polygon.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'RiskMap_prediction'
to_table(
  object,
  label = NULL,
  aggregate = NULL,
  summaries = NULL,
  quantity = "response",
  sort_by = NULL,
  digits = 1,
  col_names = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A RiskMap_prediction object from predict.RiskMap() with boundaries.

label

Name of the column of the boundaries used to name the rows. By default, the first character or factor column, or the polygon number when there is none.

aggregate

Aggregations to include, such as "mean" or "sum". By default, all those calculated.

summaries

Summaries to include, such as "mean", "exceedance" or "sd". By default, all those calculated.

quantity

Predictive quantity to tabulate. Defaults to "response".

sort_by

Name of a summary, such as "mean", used to sort the rows in decreasing order, using the first aggregation that has it. By default, rows keep the order of the boundaries.

digits

Number of decimal places for values that are not counts.

col_names

Optional column names, replacing the default headers.

...

Additional arguments passed to knitr::kable().

Value

An object of class knitr_kable.

Details

Each aggregation gives one or more columns. When the predictive mean and both interval limits are available, they are combined in one column as "mean (lower to upper)". Exceedance probabilities are omitted for sums of a probability, because the thresholds refer to the probability itself. Probabilities, including prevalence averaged over a polygon and exceedance probabilities, are shown as percentages. Sums are shown to three significant digits with thousands separators. The default headers name the quantity as in the maps drawn by plot.RiskMap_prediction().

See also

predict.RiskMap(), plot.RiskMap_prediction()

Examples

data(italy_sim)
example_data <- italy_sim[1:50, ]
fit <- glgpm(y ~ gp(), data = example_data, family = "gaussian",
             messages = FALSE)
areas <- sf::st_sf(name = c("West", "East"),
                   geometry = sf::st_make_grid(example_data, n = c(2, 1)))
prediction <- predict(fit, newdata = example_data, boundaries = areas,
                      aggregate = "mean",
                      summaries = c("mean", "lower", "upper"),
                      messages = FALSE)
#> Warning: The conditional prediction covariance of 2 of 2 blocks needed a diagonal
#> jitter, of up to 1e-12, to be factorised.
to_table(prediction)
#> 
#> 
#> |Area | Mean y (95% interval)|
#> |:----|---------------------:|
#> |West |    10.0 (9.8 to 10.1)|
#> |East |      9.6 (9.4 to 9.8)|
